title: Charred Pan Naan with Yoghurt and Ghee
summary: A soft yoghurt and ghee dough is shaped into teardrops, cooked wet side down in a very hot cast-iron pan, charred over a flame and brushed with ghee.
equipment: heavy cast-iron frying pan or tawa

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
ghee or butter, melted, to brush

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Stir the flour, yeast, sugar, salt and baking powder together. Add the yoghurt, water and 2 tbsp ghee and mix to a soft, slightly sticky dough. Knead 5 minutes until smooth.

steps.title: Rise
steps.text: Cover and leave 1.5-2 hours until doubled.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Cut into 8 pieces, roll into balls and rest 10 minutes. Roll or stretch each into a teardrop about 22 cm long and 5 mm thick.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Heat the pan over high heat for 3 minutes. Brush the top of a naan with water and lay it wet side down. Cook 1-1.5 minutes until big bubbles rise and the base is charred in spots.

steps.title: Char
steps.text: Flip and cook 1 minute more, or hold the bubbled side over a gas flame for a few seconds until it blisters.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Brush at once with melted ghee and wrap in a tea towel while you cook the rest. Serve hot.

tips: The pan must be very hot before the first naan goes in, or it dries out instead of puffing.
Wetting the top helps the naan grip the pan, just as it sticks to a tandoor wall.
A soft, slightly sticky dough gives the lightest naan; resist adding extra flour.
storage: Keep wrapped at room temperature and eat within 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month. Refresh in a hot oven for a few minutes. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
